questions.question: How much blood is in a typical adult's body?
questions.fact: Men and women carry about the same share of their body weight as blood, 7 to 8%.

questions.question: How many bones are in an adult human skeleton?
questions.fact: Babies are born with around 270; some of them fuse together on the way to adulthood.

questions.question: How many nerve cells are in the human brain?
questions.fact: The whole adult brain weighs only about 1.2 to 1.4 kg, around 2% of the body's weight.

questions.question: How much air does an adult take in with one breath?
questions.fact: British rower Pete Reed is reported to have the largest lung capacity on record, 11.68 litres.

questions.question: How tall was Robert Wadlow, the tallest person ever recorded?
questions.fact: He weighed 199 kg when he died, aged 22.

questions.question: How long is a giraffe's tongue?
questions.fact: It's black, perhaps against sunburn, and grabs food from branches straight above when the giraffe tips its head back.

questions.question: How long was the longest blue whale ever scientifically measured?
questions.fact: A stranded blue whale's heart weighed 180 kg, the largest known heart of any animal.

questions.question: How long does an African bush elephant's pregnancy last?
questions.fact: It's the longest pregnancy of any mammal.

questions.question: How many legs does the leggiest millipede on record have?
questions.fact: It was the first millipede found with over 1,000 legs, and its name, Eumillipes, means 'true thousand feet'.

questions.question: What is the world's chicken population?
questions.fact: More than 50 billion are raised every year for meat and eggs.

questions.question: How old was the oldest Greenland shark ever dated?
questions.fact: Greenland sharks only reach maturity at around 150 years old.

questions.question: How tall is the Eiffel Tower?
questions.fact: It was the tallest human-made structure in the world for 41 years, until New York's Chrysler Building in 1930.

questions.question: How tall is the Statue of Liberty?
questions.definition: ground to torch tip, pedestal included
questions.fact: The copper statue itself is 46 metres to the torch; the pedestal and foundation make up the other half.

questions.question: How long is the Great Wall of China, counting all its sections?
questions.fact: The wall built under the Ming dynasty accounts for 8,850 km of it.

questions.question: How tall is the Burj Khalifa?
questions.fact: Almost a third of that is a spire with very little usable space: without it, the tower would stand 585 metres tall.

questions.question: What is the population of New York City?
questions.fact: An estimated 800 languages are spoken there, making it the most linguistically diverse city in the world.

questions.question: What is the area of Vatican City?
questions.fact: That makes it the world's smallest country, and with about 882 residents, the least populous too.

questions.question: How far away is the Moon?
questions.fact: It is spiralling away from Earth by about 3.8 cm a year.

questions.question: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.fact: Getting out of the Sun is the slow part: light from its centre can take 10,000 to 170,000 years to reach the surface.

questions.question: How long does the International Space Station take to circle Earth once?
questions.fact: It travels at about 27,600 km/h, a little over 400 km up.

questions.question: How many people walked on the Moon during the Apollo program?
questions.fact: Nobody who landed there ever went back for a second time.

questions.question: How deep is the Challenger Deep, the deepest known point in the ocean?
questions.fact: Two men first reached the bottom in 1960, in the bathyscaphe Trieste.

questions.question: How tall is Angel Falls in Venezuela, the world's tallest waterfall?
questions.fact: Its biggest single plunge is 807 metres.

questions.question: How many flashes of lightning happen on Earth every second?
questions.fact: That adds up to nearly 1.4 billion flashes a year.

questions.question: How many trees are there on Earth?
questions.fact: That's 46% fewer than when farming began, 12,000 years ago.

questions.question: How fast does sound travel through air?
questions.fact: Through iron it goes almost 15 times faster.

questions.question: How much does a cubic metre of air weigh?
questions.fact: That is still about 800 times lighter than the same volume of water.

questions.question: How many elements are known to science?
questions.fact: Only the first 94 have been found occurring naturally on Earth.

questions.question: How many flowers does it take to make one kilogram of saffron?
questions.fact: Picking them by hand takes about forty hours.

questions.question: How much does a typical wheel of Parmigiano Reggiano weigh?
questions.fact: It takes a lot of milk: each 1,100-litre vat makes just two wheels.

questions.question: How hot must the oven be for a true Neapolitan pizza?
questions.fact: At that heat the pizza bakes in 60 to 90 seconds.

questions.question: What weight of tomatoes was thrown at Spain's La Tomatina festival?
questions.fact: It's thrown by up to 20,000 ticket holders, in a town of about 9,000 people.

questions.question: How long is a standard bank card?
questions.fact: It's the ID-1 card size, 85.60 by 53.98 mm, which most ID cards use too.

questions.question: How many passengers is an Airbus A380 certified to carry?
questions.fact: In the evacuation test, everyone got out in 78 seconds with half the exits blocked.

questions.question: How much water does an Olympic swimming pool hold?
questions.fact: The rules set no maximum depth, so as a unit of volume it's only ever approximate.

questions.question: How long is a marathon?
questions.fact: The distance was fixed in 1921, copied from the course of the 1908 London Olympics.

questions.question: How high is a basketball hoop?
questions.definition: to the top of the rim
questions.fact: The first baskets were peach baskets nailed to a gym balcony; metal hoops replaced them in 1906.

questions.question: How much gold is in an Olympic gold medal?
questions.fact: The rest of the medal is at least 92.5% silver.

questions.question: How long did the longest professional tennis match last?
questions.fact: John Isner beat Nicolas Mahut 70-68 in the fifth set, after 11 hours 5 minutes spread over three days.

source.title: Isner–Mahut match at the 2010 Wimbledon Championships

questions.question: How many keys does a modern piano have?
questions.fact: In Mozart's day pianos had five octaves; today's 88 keys span more than seven.

questions.question: How tall is the Mona Lisa?
questions.fact: It's painted on wood, not canvas: a poplar panel 77 by 53 cm.

questions.question: How many performances did The Phantom of the Opera give on Broadway?
questions.fact: It closed in 2023 as Broadway's longest-running show, by over 3,500 performances.

source.title: The Phantom of the Opera (1986 musical)

questions.question: How much beer does the Czech Republic drink per person each year?
questions.fact: No country drinks more; Austria comes second, at about 108 litres.

source.title: List of countries by beer consumption per capita

questions.question: How much tea does Turkey get through per person each year?
questions.fact: No country drinks more; Ireland comes second, at 2.36 kg.

source.title: List of countries by tea consumption per capita

questions.question: How many people can the world's biggest stadium hold?
questions.fact: North Korea's Rungrado 1st of May Stadium is next, at 113,281.

questions.question: What is the area of the Caspian Sea, the world's largest lake?
questions.fact: Lake Superior, the next largest, is only about a fifth of its size.
